record.title: China proposes new technology export catalog entries and interim registration for AI exports
record.summary: On 2026-10-16, China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology issued Announcement No. 48, proposing changes to the technology export catalog and opening consultation through 2026-11-15. The proposal covers 40 technologies across AI, biomedicine and photovoltaics, including 23 AI-related entries. Draft Annex 1 names categories spanning malware generation/evasion, vulnerability discovery, models and agents, chip design and compute clusters, with technical indicators for multiple entries. China’s official 2023 catalog already restricted some AI-related or adjacent technologies, including language-specific AI interaction interfaces, intelligent grading, recommendation systems, vulnerability discovery/mining and malicious-code programming; this partial baseline does not establish exact overlap with every 2026 proposal. The 2026 announcement also states interim pre-export registration pending formal revision. MOFCOM's Q&A describes public-domain exclusions, licensing paths and distinctions between covered overseas local deployment and API/app/SaaS/lightweight on-device services. Annex classifications, complete crosswalk, final adoption, case-specific applicability and implementation effects remain unresolved.
organizations: Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China
Ministry of Science and Technology of the People's Republic of China

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology published Announcement No. 48 on 2026-10-16, opened consultation on proposed revisions to the technology export catalog, and announced an interim pre-export registration measure.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The announcement describes proposed entries across 40 technologies in artificial intelligence, biomedicine and photovoltaics, including 23 AI-related entries concerning large models, agents, computing clusters and information processing. It states that AI technologies already in the public domain through open source or academic publication are not included in the proposed scope.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: From the announcement date until the formal catalog revision takes effect, exporters must register before exporting technologies listed in the announcement; the stated cases include transfer of ownership, licensing use abroad and a change of ownership or effective control to a foreign entity. The announcement also describes expedited or automatic licensing pathways for specified AI-related activities.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The consultation is open through 2026-11-15. Annex 1 is a draft technical schedule with item-level AI categories and quantitative control indicators, including AI malware generation/variation and adaptive evasion, AI-assisted vulnerability discovery, model and agent technologies, chip design and compute-cluster technologies. This text extraction does not establish row classification, final adoption or case-specific legal applicability.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In its official Q&A, MOFCOM states that after formal implementation, overseas local deployment of covered restricted AI technology falls within technology-export management, while API calls, app/web interaction, SaaS and lightweight on-device deployment using restricted large models are outside large-model technology export management. This is the ministry's stated interpretation, not a case-specific legal ruling.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The attached draft Annex 1 names specific AI technology categories and provides technical indicators for multiple entries, spanning offensive cyber capabilities, model and agent systems, AI-chip design and large-scale compute clusters. The indicators are proposed consultation text; this inspection did not resolve every table classification or interpret applicability to any particular export.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: China's official 2023 catalog already restricted certain AI-related or adjacent technologies. Under information-processing technology it listed language-specific AI interaction interfaces, intelligent grading and personalized information-push/recommendation systems; a separate information-countermeasure entry covered vulnerability discovery/mining and malicious-code programming/implantation. This shows prior controls existed, but does not establish item-by-item overlap with every 2026 draft entry or that all proposed thresholds are new.

evidence_gaps.description: Annex 1 was text-inspected, but extraction did not preserve all table layout/column mappings needed to assign every 2026 AI indicator to a precise proposed classification. The official 2023 catalog contains existing AI-related and adjacent entries, but a complete item-by-item crosswalk to the 2026 proposal has not been established.
No final catalog amendment, transition notice, implementation record, or public data about registrations and enforcement was inspected.

brief.importance_rationale: If adopted and applied to the covered model, agent, cyber and compute technologies, the proposal could change cross-border transfer and collaboration across several AI research and infrastructure activities. Its technical criteria and public-domain, licensing and service exceptions narrow that consequence; the draft does not establish a general export ban or realized economic effects.
limitations: The catalog revision is proposed and consultation was open through 2026-11-15; the permanent amended catalog is not established by these sources.

The draft WPS Annex 1 was retrieved and text-inspected, exposing specific categories and technical indicators. The extraction did not preserve the full table layout/column mapping, and this review does not determine whether a specific technology or transaction is legally covered.
The measure is described as interim pre-export registration until the amended catalog takes effect. No registration, enforcement, denial or export-impact data were reviewed.

MOFCOM's official Q&A says API calls, app/web interaction, SaaS and lightweight on-device interactions using a restricted large model are outside large-model technology export management, while overseas local deployment of covered restricted technology is within scope after formal implementation; this is the ministry's stated interpretation, not a case-specific legal determination.
The stated public-domain exclusion and specified automatic or expedited licensing provisions narrow or qualify the proposed controls; this is not evidence of a general AI export ban.

The official 2023 catalog already includes some AI-related or adjacent restrictions (language-specific AI interaction interfaces, intelligent grading, recommendation systems, vulnerability discovery/mining and malicious-code programming/implantation). This partial thematic comparison does not prove item-by-item overlap or establish that every 2026 proposed threshold is new.

technical.claimed_result: The official notice proposes catalog additions plus interim pre-export registration. Draft Annex 1 names AI categories including malware generation/evasion, vulnerability discovery, model/agent technologies, chip design and compute clusters, with technical indicators. The 2023 catalog already covers some AI-related or adjacent technologies; exact overlap and the classification of each 2026 draft row remain unresolved.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official notice and FAQ document publication and the announced policy text; they do not establish final adoption of the proposed permanent catalog changes or measurable enforcement effects.
technical.implementation_status: Consultation opened 2026-10-16 and runs through 2026-11-15. Interim pre-export registration is stated to apply from publication until the formal revision takes effect. Annex 1 is draft text; no registration or enforcement outcomes were reviewed.
technical.mechanism: Consultation on proposed catalog additions plus temporary registration before export of listed technologies. The notice and Q&A describe public-domain carve-outs, specified automatic licensing pathways and distinctions among transfer, overseas local deployment and model-access services.

Annex 1 lists technical categories and indicators; applicable transactions, classifications and final legal scope remain subject to consultation and interpretation.
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable as a policy announcement; verify the enacted final catalog, annex text and subsequent implementation records.
technical.strongest_baseline: China's official 2023 prohibited/restricted technology catalog and subsequent amendments; the 2023 text already lists language-specific AI interaction interfaces, intelligent grading, personalized recommendation, vulnerability discovery/mining and malicious-code programming/implantation. No full item-by-item crosswalk to the proposed 2026 Annex 1 has been completed.

brief.title: China proposes new technology export catalog entries and interim registration for AI exports
brief.why_it_matters: If adopted and applied, the proposal could affect cross-border transfer and collaboration involving selected AI, cyber, chip-design and compute-cluster capabilities. The draft Annex makes the proposed scope more concrete through named categories and technical indicators. Because the 2023 catalog already covered some AI-related and adjacent technologies, the 2026 change should be understood as proposed additions and more specific controls, not the first AI-related export controls; exact overlap remains unresolved. Public-domain, licensing and service exceptions also narrow what can be inferred. No registrations, enforcement or economic effects are established.
